crash.page_caption: Market regime detection based on the S&P 500 (SPY)
crash.intro_desc: The crash early warning system detects market regimes using an Isolation Forest model (machine learning) trained on S&P 500 data. The traffic light shows the current regime (Green/Yellow/Red), and the Risk Score (0–100) quantifies the anomaly strength. Below you can see the historical score chart with colour-coded regime phases and a backtest showing how the market typically performs after high scores.
crash.backtest_desc: Risk Score (0–100) for each trading day. Green < 40, Yellow 40–69, Red ≥ 70. Computed via Isolation Forest (sklearn).
crash.section_polymarket: Polymarket Macro Risk — What the Market Is Pricing In
crash.polymarket_desc: Our Isolation Forest model measures the regime from price data. Polymarket shows what traders are pricing in based on events — two distinct signals. When both are red, confidence in the risk call increases. Divergence (e.g. low Risk Score but high Recession market) is itself a signal.

wt.month_filter_hint: Applies to all weekday sections except heatmaps
wt.cumulative_week_desc: Shows how the weekly return builds from Monday to Friday. The yellow line shows the current week for comparison. If the curve rises mainly at the start of the week, this suggests early buying pressure (e.g. institutional allocation on Monday).
wt.avg_return_winrate_title: Average Return & Win Rate per Weekday
wt.overnight_intraday_desc: Breaks down the daily return into Overnight (yesterday's close → today's open) and Intraday (open → close). If the return comes mainly overnight, buy-and-hold investors benefit. If intraday dominates, active trading is relevant.
wt.consecutive_desc: Probability that the following day is positive, depending on whether the previous day was positive (↑) or negative (↓). Values above 55% indicate trend continuation, below 45% mean reversion.
wt.quarterly_heatmap_desc: Shows whether weekday effects vary seasonally. E.g. the Monday effect may only be significant in Q4 (window dressing, year-end rally), while disappearing in Q2/Q3.
wt.weekend_effect_desc: Measures the return over the weekend (Friday close → Monday open, residual method). Historically a negative weekend effect is often observed for equities — Mondays open below Friday's close.

svb.page_caption: Rolling regression between spot returns and implied volatility changes
svb.intro_desc: This page shows the statistical relationship between daily spot returns and changes in implied volatility. A negative beta (typical) means: when the market rises, the VIX falls — and vice versa. Regime turning points mark extremes in this relationship.
svb.daily_beta_note: Green bars = positive beta (unusual), red bars = negative beta (normal). The rolling beta measures the current sensitivity of the spot to vol changes.
svb.vol_regime_buckets: Vol-Regime Buckets: ∅ Return per VIX Level
svb.vol_buckets_note: Average spot return on days when the vol index was in the respective range. High-vol regimes often show asymmetric return distributions.
svb.vrp_summary: Volatility Risk Premium: Implied vs. Realized Vol
svb.vrp_note: The VRP measures how much investors pay for protection (implied vol) above the realized historical vol. A positive VRP is the normal state — the market prices in a safety premium.
svb.regime_turning_points: Regime Turning Points: What Happens After Extremes?
opex.page_caption: Seasonal patterns around the monthly options expiration (3rd Friday) & Triple Witching
opex.intro_desc: OPEX (Options Expiration) is the monthly options expiration on the 3rd Friday. In quarterly months (March, June, September, December) futures also expire — the so-called Triple Witching. Here you analyze how the market typically behaves around these dates: return path, volatility, monthly breakdown and backtest. Sidebar: Choose ticker, period and event window — all sections update automatically.
opex.triple_witching_section: Triple Witching — Path Around the Expiration Day
opex.monthly_section: Monthly Expiration — 12 Charts (one chart per month)
opex.significance_section: Significance Test — Is the Effect Statistically Meaningful?
opex.vixpiration_para: VIXpiration dates are shown in the OPEX calendar for reference. Detailed VIXpiration analysis with dedicated charts, backtest and significance test: VIXpiration page →
vix.page_caption: Seasonal patterns around the VIX settlement date (calendar 3rd Fri − 30 days, CBOE rule)
vix.intro_desc: The VIX expiration (VIXpiration) occurs monthly — 30 calendar days before the 3rd Friday (CBOE rule). Here you see how the market typically behaves around this date: average return path, volatility patterns, significance tests and a backtest of the VIX strategy. Sidebar: Set ticker, period and event window (t−x to t+y) — all sections update automatically.
ki.page_caption: Recalibrated seasonal path (TruePath) + AI Composite Score 1–10
ki.intro_desc: AI Seasonality combines classical seasonal analysis with machine learning. The TruePath finds the historically most similar years (correlation/DTW) and projects their weighted path into the future. The AI Composite Score (0–10) combines four sub-scores into a single signal: match quality, forward return, monthly win rate and tracking quality.
bt.intro_desc: The Backtest Engine tests seasonal trading strategies on historical data. Choose an event (FOMC, OPEX, holiday, calendar day…), define entry/exit offsets and examine the equity curve, win rate and significance. 4 tabs: Single backtest, grid optimisation (all parameter combinations), walk-forward analysis (out-of-sample) and event relevance ranking. Sidebar: Ticker, period, event type, offsets, stop-loss and indicator filters — all combinable.
bt.wf_desc: Optimised on in-sample, tested on out-of-sample → realistic performance without overfitting.
bt.relevance_desc: Which events are statistically significant? t-test + effect size (Cohen's d) + win rate → relevance score.
bt.how_to_read_score: 📖 How to Read the Relevance Score
bt.score_intro: The relevance score combines three dimensions into an overall value between 0 and 1:
bt.score_legend: t-statistic: Signal strength vs. null. |t| > 2 = robust effect. p-value: Probability of chance. p < 0.05 = significant. Cohen's d: Effect size. d > 0.5 = medium, d > 0.8 = large.
bt.backtest_logic_desc: Each event date defines a trade: entry = event_date − days_before trading days, exit = event_date + days_after trading days. Minimum gap between trades = 5 days (prevents overlap).
bt.wf_method_desc: Expanding window: optimise on the past, test on the future. Each fold runs a grid search on in-sample years, then applies the best parameters to out-of-sample years. The aggregated OOS performance is the most honest estimate of live performance.
bt.relevance_score_desc: One t-test per event (H0: mean = 0). Score = 50% significance (1−p) + 30% win rate + 20% effect size (Cohen's d, capped at 1.0).
pm.page_caption: Prediction market data as a second frame of reference alongside seasonality. Live via Polymarket Gamma + CLOB API.
pm.intro_desc: Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market. Traders stake real money (USDC) on specific outcomes — Fed decisions, recession, BTC price surges. The YES price between 0 and 1 directly reflects the implied market probability: 0.34 means the market sees a 34% chance for the outcome. Here you compare these collective market expectations with historical seasonality — three perspectives emerge: 1) Fed Path 2026 as a distribution over 0–12+ cuts, 2) Risk Traffic Light for tail events (recession, hike, emergency cut), 3) Crypto Divergence between the historical prior and market price. Sidebar: Filter by category, choose history period, select up to 10 markets for the explorer.
pm.fed_path_caption: 13 outcome markets from the Polymarket event "How many Fed rate cuts in 2026?". Each bar shows the implied market probability for exactly that many cuts. The expected value (green line) is the probability-weighted sum.
pm.fed_dist_hint: How to read this chart: each bar is a separate Polymarket market — e.g. "Will the Fed cut exactly 3 times in 2026?". The height shows how much probability the market assigns to that outcome. The gold bar marks the most probable scenario. The green dashed line is the expected value — the probability-weighted average across all outcomes. Example: if it sits at 1.3, the market expects about 1.3 cuts on average, roughly 33 basis points of total reduction in 2026.
pm.fed_trend_hint: How to read this chart: each line shows the probability history of one outcome. Steep lines = rapid market repricing, typically after FOMC meetings or CPI prints. When "0 cuts" rises while "2 cuts" falls, the market is pricing in a hawkish shift. The opposite = dovish shift.
pm.risk_signal_caption: Four binary markets for scenarios outside the Fed baseline path. Red: historically elevated probability. Green: market sees this as unlikely.
pm.risk_signal_hint: How to read the traffic light: each tile shows a binary market (YES/NO). The percentage is the current implied probability for the YES outcome. Green = unusually low, neutral = baseline level, red = significantly elevated. Thresholds: Recession > 35% (red), Fed hike > 20%, emergency cut > 15%, negative GDP > 15%.
pm.risk_history_hint: How to read this chart: time history of the four risk markets. Correlated moves (all rising together) signal a genuine regime shift. Divergences (e.g. recession rising but negative GDP stays flat) point to market-specific news rather than general macro concern.
pm.crypto_div_caption: Horizontal ladders of price targets through end of 2026. Compare the market probabilities with your seasonal forecasts on the respective ticker pages.
pm.crypto_ladder_hint: How to read the ladder: each horizontal bar is a Polymarket for "will the price reach at least X by end of 2026?". The higher the price target, the lower the probability. The bar directly shows the implied market probability in percent. Typical reading: BTC ≥ $100k: 40% means the market sees a 40% chance that Bitcoin closes the year above $100k.
pm.divergence_caption: For each crypto target: the seasonal prior empirically calculated from price history (share of past years with a year-end return ≥ required performance from today). Compared to the current Polymarket probability. Green: seasonality higher than market (market underestimates). Red: seasonality lower than market.
pm.divergence_table_hint: How to read the table: Required = percentage return the current price still needs to reach the target by year-end. Market YES = current Polymarket probability. Seasonal Prior = share of past years in which this return from today's calendar date to year-end was actually achieved. Divergence = Seasonal Prior minus Market YES in percentage points. Positive (green): seasonality predicts a higher chance than the market — possible long trade if fundamentals align. Negative (red): market prices in more optimism than history justifies — caution.
pm.explorer_caption: Select up to 10 markets in the sidebar to compare their price paths. Divergences between markets reveal regime shifts (e.g. "no cuts" falls while "2 cuts" rises = market pricing in a dovish shift).
pm.explorer_hint: How to read this chart: all selected markets in one chart. Y-axis = probability in percent (0–100). Display mode: everything rising or falling together = shared market theme (e.g. all cut outcomes rising = dovish regime shift). Crossing lines between related markets often mark important repricing days (CPI, FOMC, jobs report).
pm.all_markets_caption: 26 markets from 7 Polymarket events. Click column headers to sort.
pm.all_markets_hint: How to read the table: YES = current implied probability. 7d Δ = change versus the price 7 days ago in percentage points — positive values = market becoming more bullish on the outcome, negative = more bearish. Liquidity = volume in the active order book in USDC. Markets with < $20k liquidity are illiquid and their prices may be distorted — prefer more liquid markets for signals. Click column headers to sort.
pm.calibration_caption: Brier score analysis on historically resolved markets. When Polymarket says 70%, does the event actually occur in ~70% of cases?
pm.calibration_hint: How to read the curve: X = predicted probability (bucketed into 10 bins). Y = actually observed hit rate in that bucket. The grey diagonal is the perfect forecaster. Points above the diagonal: market underestimates — the event occurs more often than stated. Points below: market overestimates.
pm.time_resolution_hint: Hypothesis: The closer the resolution date, the better the Brier score should get — more information available, less uncertainty. A flat trend means: Polymarket already knows the outcome months in advance.
div.intro_desc: Analyses price behaviour around the ex-dividend date: pre-ex-date drift (dividend capture premium), the price drop on the ex-date and the subsequent recovery. The event window shows the average pattern across all historical dividend dates.
div.page_caption: Price behaviour around the ex-dividend date
div.event_window_desc: Normalised to the price on the ex-date (t0 = 0%). Positive = above the ex-date price.
div.monthly_dist_desc: Number of ex-dividend dates per calendar month over the selected period.
div.methodik_source: Price data from the SeasonAlpha database (Supabase, updated daily). Ex-dividend dates and amounts from Yahoo Finance.
div.methodik_t0_desc: On this day the stock already trades without the dividend (ex-dividend). In efficient markets the price drop on the ex-date approximately equals the dividend amount.
div.methodik_normierung: All historical event windows are normalised to the closing price on the ex-date (t0 = 0%) and averaged. Events with incomplete windows (too close to the start or end of the data) are excluded.
div.methodik_capture: The strategy buys shortly before the ex-date and sells afterwards. The pre-ex drift and post-ex recovery determine profitability net of transaction costs.
earn.intro_desc: Analyses price behaviour and volatility around quarterly earnings: pre-earnings drift (price run-up before the release), the earnings-day move, post-earnings drift and the vola crush (decline in price fluctuation after the announcement). Where available: Beat vs. Miss breakdown.
earn.data_availability_desc: Currently supported: US stocks (4 quarters per run, growing daily to up to 16 within a year). Indices, futures, crypto and ETFs have no earnings. European and Asian equities will follow once we connect a suitable data source.
earn.page_caption: Price movement & volatility around quarterly results
earn.event_window_desc: Normalised to the closing price on earnings day (t0 = 0%). Positive = above the earnings close.
earn.vola_title: Volatility Before & After Earnings — Vola Crush
earn.vola_desc: Average absolute daily return (realised vol) per trading day in the event window. The typical rise before earnings and the vola crush afterwards are clearly visible.
earn.methodik_source: Price data from the SeasonAlpha database. Earnings dates and EPS data from Yahoo Finance (historical quarterly results).
earn.methodik_t0_desc: (date of the quarterly results release). After-market reports are typically reflected in the price of the next trading day — this effect is visible in the t0/t+1 move.
earn.methodik_normierung: All event windows are normalised to the t0 closing price. Positive values mean: price above the earnings close.
earn.methodik_beat_miss: "Beat" = EPS actual > EPS estimate; "Miss" = EPS actual < EPS estimate. Only available when Yahoo Finance provides EPS data.
earn.methodik_vola_crush: Measured as the average absolute daily return (|Δ%|) per day in the window. The typical rise before earnings (driven by uncertainty) and the decline afterwards (vola crush once uncertainty is resolved) are a well-known pattern in options markets.
earn.methodik_realized_vola: Realised vol before earnings = avg |daily return| in the t-before trading days. Realised vol after earnings = avg |daily return| in the t-after trading days (t0 excluded).
risk.intro_desc: The risk side of the seasonal cycle: when during the year do the largest pullbacks (drawdowns) typically occur? How high is rolling volatility throughout the year? And does the risk profile differ by presidential cycle phase? Sidebar: set the period and vol window — all sections update automatically.
risk.methodik_normierung: Each year starts at 100. Daily returns compound: value = 100 × exp(Σ log_return)
risk.methodik_interpolation_desc: Each annual curve is interpolated to 365 calendar days
risk.methodik_avg_dd_desc: Drawdown calculated per year, then averaged across all years
risk.methodik_rolling_vola_desc: Annualised std of log returns over a rolling window (√252 annualisation)
risk.methodik_cross_year_desc: The rolling calculation concatenates all years so that January values correctly draw on prior-December data
risk.methodik_percentile_desc: "In what % of years was vol lower on the same day than today?"

scan.method_data_source: Data source: The Seasonal Scanner runs nightly across all supported tickers and calculates an AI Seasonality Score on a scale of 0–10 for each. The score combines 4 sub-scores: DTW pattern matching, Prophet forecast, win rate for the current month, and tracking quality (correlation to the historical pattern).
scan.method_win_rate: Win Rate = percentage of historical years in which the current month was positive.
scan.method_avg_return: Avg. Return = average monthly return for the current calendar month across all available years.
scan.method_update_note: Note: The scanner updates all tickers only on full runs (several times per week depending on server load, not necessarily daily). The scan date shown above reflects the actual data timestamp.
scan.method_disclaimer: Not investment advice. The signals shown are purely statistical-historical analyses and do not constitute a buy recommendation.

sig.p_value_desc: Probability of a random result (p<0.05 = significant)
pmjs.seasonal_prior_desc: Seasonal Prior = % of past years with Year-End ≥ required return from today.
